approvalScope: One architectural requirement in one patch record. This approves no route, no packet, no price and no deployment. It changes where the checkout defense is required to live; it does not change what a caller observes, and it opens nothing that was closed.
note: A successor act, recorded rather than applied silently. The superseded requirement is preserved verbatim below and the prior applied digest is retained in the patch record's priorAppliedSha256, so a later reader can see what was approved before, what replaced it, and on whose authority.
decisionSource: Explicit owner instruction, recorded verbatim in decisionText.

supersedes.requiredBehaviorVerbatim: After item ownership resolution and before sponsored/payment handling, resolve the item's exact track metadata. Return 403 with no checkout URL/session/amount for component_deferral. Keep the payment-adapter denial as a second independent guard.
supersedes.supersededClause: Keep the payment-adapter denial as a second independent guard.
supersedes.clauseRetained: Return 403 with no checkout URL/session/amount for component_deferral. The outcome clause is unchanged and still required.

decisionText: The current consolidated protected-authority architecture replaces the old c-deferral-checkout-route-defense requirement for a separate route-level track guard in checkout/route.ts. APPROVE the consolidated architecture as the successor. The requirement that checkout/route.ts maintain a separate independent track-resolution guard is superseded. The payment-adapter/protected-authority path is the authoritative checkout defense. The outcome is preserved, the old mechanism was deliberately consolidated, and the current protection is mutation-proven. Keeping the obsolete second-independent-guard requirement would force duplicate logic back into the checkout route for no demonstrated safety gain.

successorImplementation.commitSubject: fix: enforce protected packet commerce authority
successorImplementation.whatItDid: Removed 46 lines from src/app/api/expungement-ai/checkout/route.ts — the route-level refusals for exact_supported_deferral, terminal_treatment_candidate and component_deferral — consolidating them into the protected authority. The route now resolves ownership, rejects partner-sponsored items, calls createConsumerPacketCheckout, and maps ConsumerCheckoutNotAllowedError to a 403 carrying no URL, session or amount.

evidenceRelieduponAtDecisionTime.outcomeClauseHolds: A component_deferral checkout request still ends in 403 with no checkout URL, session or amount.
evidenceRelieduponAtDecisionTime.verifierResult: 2777 checks over the exact ten routes and thirty-one components the patches targeted, EN+ES.
evidenceRelieduponAtDecisionTime.verifierNominatedBy: captainApplication in the patch spec itself, so the test of whether the approved behaviour still holds is the one the approval named.

whatThisDoesNotDecide: It does not approve any route, packet family, price or commercial surface.
It does not authorize a deployment, a migration, an environment change or a Stripe live-mode call.
It does not reach any other patch in the c-dependency spec. The other ten remain as their own reconstruction recorded them.
It does not re-freeze data/rcap-all50/review-artifacts/c-dependency-correction-assignment.json, whose own SHA-256 is pinned separately and which needs its own authority.
It makes no statement about packet_credit_admission, which no approved requirement ever obliged to refuse independently.
